messages:
maria: Heads-up — onboarding smoke for the ruby minimal sample app is flaking during token refresh. 401 on the first request ~60% of runs. anyone seen this?
jon: ugh saw this locally yesterday. seems like race when the refresh token gets swapped and the client uses stale header for the first stream chunk.
maria: repro steps: run `bundle exec ruby examples/minimal.rb --refreshable-token` then immediately call /generate. sometimes returns 401, then subsequent retries succeed.
lee: can you paste the client init snippet? might be the header caching.
maria: sure — minimal snippet:
```
client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'], use_refreshable: true)
resp = client.generate(prompt: 'hello')
```
I think the client pre-computes the Authorization header once and we race replacing the token.
jon: yeah that matches. our Ruby SDK caches headers in the connection adapter to avoid per-request string allocations. fails when token replacer mutates ENV mid-flight.
olivia: quick thought: should the SDK lock during token refresh or just always call a proc to fetch token per request? lock adds latency but safe; proc adds overhead but simpler.
sara: for minimal sample app we should document the expected pattern for refreshable tokens (provide a lambda) and add test coverage for refresh race.
maria: opened PR with a small change to call a token_proc per request when use_refreshable: true — ~3 LOC. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sampleapp/pull/42
rb-ci-bot: CI: ruby-sampleapp / minimal-onboard smoke — failure on matrix job ruby-3.1 (flaky 401) — rerun queued.
jon: I skimmed the PR — looks fine but let's add a unit test that simulates concurrent requests during refresh. otherwise we'll regress.
maria: added a basic thread-based test that swaps token mid-request, pushed commit 2.
lee: can we also add a short note to docs/quickstart.md about using token lambdas and a recommended pattern: 
```
client = Redwood::Client.new { fetch_fresh_token }
```
so users don't pass ENV directly.
olivia: +1 to doc note. for Dedicated customers this could cause subtle 401s in short bursts.
sara: also consider a small changelog entry in the gem release notes so folks see the behavioral change.
maria: will add changelog and squash commits. thanks for quick triage :thumbsup:
jon: once CI green i'll merge and backport to the maintenance branch.
lee: follow-up: maybe we should add an opt-in config to re-enable header caching for ultra-low-latency apps and document the tradeoff.
maria: opened an issue to track caching opt-in: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sampleapp/issues/58
olivia: sweet. this was small but good catch.
maria: closing the loop — CI green, merged, changelog included. thanks team! :tada:
